quote: Section 14.2 of the Supply Agreement provides that any change in direct or indirect ownership of more than 50% of Customer's outstanding voting stock "shall be deemed an assignment of this Agreement by Customer and shall require the prior written consent of Supplier. If any such change occurs without the prior written consent of Supplier, Supplier may terminate this Agreement upon thirty (30) days' written notice to Customer." This transaction is a 100% change in ownership. Vantrell's consent is therefore required. Yet Schedule 4.4 of the Disclosure Schedule states "None," ... Section 7.2(c) makes it a condition to Closing that "all consents, approvals and notices set forth on Schedule 4.4 shall have been received." Because Schedule 4.4 says "None," that condition is automatically satisfied.
reason: The memo identifies the Supply Agreement Section 14.2 provision: a change of more than 50% ownership is deemed an assignment, it requires Vantrell's prior written consent, and Vantrell may terminate on 30 days' notice. The memo says the 100% stock sale triggers this. It explains why the SPA does not address it: Section 4.4 and Schedule 4.4 say "None," and the Section 7.2(c) condition covers only Schedule 4.4 consents. It notes that indemnity recourse would be subject to the deductible and cap. It recommends adding the consent to Schedule 4.4 and making it a closing condition.
